name: Height stack (GH + IGF-1 + MK-677)

card.summary: A combination of growth hormone, IGF-1 and the oral growth hormone secretagogue MK-677 used by people trying to gain height.
card.note: Prescription or investigational compounds; approved use is limited to specific medical conditions in children.

quick.overview:
A height stack is a combination of growth-promoting agents, typically recombinant growth hormone (GH), IGF-1 and MK-677 (ibutamoren), that people in heightmaxxing communities use hoping to grow taller. Each acts on the GH/IGF-1 axis, which drives growth in children and adolescents.

Growth hormone therapy is approved for several short-stature conditions in children, with adult height gains of roughly 4 to 8 cm reported in trials for idiopathic short stature. No published trial has tested the combined stack for height.
quick.how: Forum posts describe stacks that pair GH with MK-677 and supporting supplements, often shared as lists for others to critique. Users usually say they are aiming at people whose growth plates are still open.
quick.risks: GH usually reduces insulin sensitivity, and MK-677 is an investigational drug not approved for human consumption. Mecasermin (IGF-1) is prescription-only and has its own side effect profile. Using these outside medical supervision is associated with documented risks.

lead: The height stack is a heightmaxxing term for combining agents that act on the growth hormone axis: recombinant growth hormone (GH), IGF-1 (the mediator of GH effects, available medically as mecasermin) and MK-677 (ibutamoren), an oral ghrelin receptor agonist.[1][2][3]

Users hope the combination raises growth factor levels enough to lengthen bones before the growth plates close, resulting in greater adult height. Forum threads show stacks shared for review, including ones from users who say their growth plates are open.[4]
Medically, GH therapy is approved for several short-stature conditions, and trials in idiopathic short stature reported gains of about 4 to 8 cm in adult height.[1]

chain: Stimulate long-bone growth at open growth plates
angle.text: Users aim to increase height by stimulating the GH/IGF-1 axis while the growth plates remain open. Medical trials of GH in children with short stature support some height gain; the combined stack has not been tested.

paras: Growth hormone therapy replaces or supplements the hormone in children with deficiency and is also FDA-approved for conditions including Turner syndrome, chronic kidney failure, Prader-Willi syndrome and idiopathic short stature (Humatrope, 2003).[1]
Mecasermin (Increlex) is recombinant IGF-1 approved for growth failure in children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, given by subcutaneous injection.[2]

MK-677 (ibutamoren) is an oral, long-acting ghrelin receptor agonist that raises GH and IGF-1 levels and also cortisol. It is an investigational drug, not approved in the US, and is used experimentally in bodybuilding and banned in most sports.[3]

Looksmax.org users post stacks for critique, usually combining GH and MK-677 with supplements such as creatine, zinc, magnesium and vitamin D; one poster in the thread states they are 16 with open plates.[4] Other threads describe AI-generated stacks, and one argues that height stacks are a "cope".[5][6]

No studies found of the combined stack for height. Trials of GH in short-stature children reported about 4 to 8 cm of adult height gain for idiopathic short stature and 5 to 8 cm for Turner syndrome.[1] MK-677 studies in healthy older adults reported raised GH and increased lean mass,[3] and a pediatric study comparing it with injectable GH is ongoing.[3]

GH generally reduces insulin sensitivity. A 2011 study found no overall cancer increase but higher risk in some subgroups, and the FDA called evidence of increased mortality inconclusive.[1] Editorials have raised concerns about off-label use in healthy people.[1]

lore.intro: Height stacks are shared on looksmax.org as lists for peer review.[4]

claims.claim: A GH + MK-677 stack can add height if plates are open
claims.believers: Posters share stacks and say they target users with open growth plates.[4]
claims.experts: GH has produced several centimetres of added adult height in trials of children with specific conditions;[1] the combination has not been studied.

claims.believers: Some members argue that no stack reliably adds height.[6]
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes GH use in healthy individuals is not supported by evidence of safety or effectiveness.[1]
